words.gloss: even if it is said to be
even if it is said that

literal: Even if it is said to be a good path, receiving is bad; even if it is said that the upper world does not exist, giving indeed is good.
translation: Even if receiving gifts is said to be a path to goodness, it is bad. Even if there is no higher world to be gained, giving to others is still the best path.
modern: பிறரிடமிருந்து பொருளைப் பெறுவது நல்ல வழி என்று சொன்னாலும் அது தீமையானது; கொடையளிப்பதால் மேலுலகம் கிடைக்காது என்றாலும் பிறருக்குக் கொடுப்பதே நல்லது.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the acts of receiving and giving to establish the supreme value of charity. The author states that accepting things from others is inherently degrading and bad, even if someone claims it is a righteous path. On the other hand, giving to those in need is inherently noble and good, even if there is no heavenly reward or higher world awaiting the giver. Virtue in giving lies in the act itself, not in the expectation of spiritual or material returns.
